content.title: About
content.content: Pork bacon is salted, smoked or cured pork belly that has been cured, optionally smoked, and sometimes pre‑cooked. It can be sold fresh, smoked, or dry‑cured, and is often ready for quick frying or grilling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bacon is a staple in many cuisines, from American breakfasts to European charcuterie boards.
Smoked bacon gets its distinctive flavor from wood smoke generated during a slow‑smoking process.
Cured bacon is typically aged for several weeks, which deepens flavor and extends shelf life.
Pork bacon is rich in protein and saturated fat, making it an energy‑dense food.
In some cultures bacon is served in ultra‑thin slices, crisped to a crunchy texture.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Bacon provides a substantial amount of complete protein needed for muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin and vitamin B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Bacon supplies iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Zinc in bacon helps immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Natural creatine can aid muscle strength and endurance.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Excessive consumption may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Bacon is salty, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Nitrites/Nitrates
items.content: Processing often uses nitrites that can form potentially harmful compounds when over‑cooked.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to pork proteins.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Bacon is very calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bacon is typically sliced thin and fried until crisp. It can be added to salads, sandwiches, soups, pasta, and potato dishes. Dry‑cured bacon can be eaten as a snack, while smoked bacon works as a flavorful garnish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bacon refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. Fresh and smoked bacon should be used within 5–7 days; cured bacon lasts up to 2 weeks. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 6 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor, discoloration, or slimy texture.
